subject: Post-call: performance validation protocol & reproducibility checklist
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@novaretail.com>, Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@novaretail.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: performance validation protocol & reproducibility checklist

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap and a proposed run plan so we have deterministic expectations for the validation run next week. Goal: confirm that the candidate model and serving profile meet NovaRetail's latency and throughput SLOs under realistic streaming load and to deliver reproducible artifacts you can audit.

Key targets (as discussed):
- Latency: p95 <= 350 ms for short completion workloads (up to 128 tokens); p95 <= 650 ms for long completions (512 tokens) when using streaming.
- Throughput: steady-state 1,200 requests/minute for the primary routing tier (mixed 60/40 short/long split).
- Concurrency: support 40 concurrent active sessions with KV cache enabled; sustained bursts to 80 for short 60s windows.
- Streaming: must deliver token-by-token flush within 25 ms of generation at the server side; client-time-to-first-token target = 100 ms.

Measurement definitions (important for reproducibility):
- Latency measured server-side (edge ingress -> final token emitted) excluding client-side parse. Report p50/p95/p99 and tail distribution with bootstrapped confidence intervals.
- Warm-up: 3 minutes continuous ramp (no measurement during warm-up).
- Sampling: use the attached prompt-set-v1.jsonl (200 prompts, labeled short/long) — fixed random seed included in the file.
- Concurrency ramp: 0->40 over 120s, hold 8 minutes, then a 60s burst to 80 for 3 cycles.
- KV cache priming: for cache-enabled runs, prime with the first 100 short prompts from the set; for a cold-cache baseline run, explicitly restart the runtime between trials.

Artifacts we'll produce and share:
- Raw harness logs (stdout + per-request timing)
- Aggregated CSV with p50/p95/p99/token counts
- A short reproducibility README showing exact Git commit, config, and invocation.

Attachments: prompt-set-v1.jsonl (prompt bundle), perf-harness-runbook.md (run commands + env), sample-results-scan.csv (example output format).

Proposed dates: Wed 2026-08-11 09:00 PT for an on-site (screen-share) run where we walk through execution and hand you the artifacts. Please confirm availability and whether you prefer us to run in our hosted environment or on your VPC test cluster (we can provide a transient test image).

Next steps / asks for you:
1) Confirm measurement targets above or flag adjustments.
2) Let us know environment choice (hosted vs VPC) and whether you need an NDA addendum for sample artifacts.
3) If you want additional edge cases (token streaming with long context churn), tell us which percent of the mix to add.

Thanks — we'll hold the slot but won't run until you confirm.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachments: prompt-set-v1.jsonl (application/jsonl), perf-harness-runbook.md (text/markdown), sample-results-scan.csv (text/csv)

From: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@novaretail.com>

Cc: Priya Kumar <priya.kumar@novaretail.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance validation protocol & reproducibility checklist

Marcus — thanks for the clear write-up. Priya and I reviewed; high level: sounds good. Two quick clarifications before we lock the run: 

1) Measurement window: when you say "hold 8 minutes" — do you report metrics across the full 8-minute window or only the last 5 minutes after a 3-minute stabilization? We typically prefer steady-state reporting over the middle window to avoid edge transients.

2) Cold-cache baseline: for our compliance team, we need a repeatable cold-cache step and the exact restart command so we can replicate inside our VPC. Can you embed that into the runbook?

Also, a privacy ask — we'll attach a short note with our data handling constraints for sample prompts (PII redaction, retention 30 days).

We are leaning to host the run in our VPC for parity with production, but if there are time constraints we can accept a hosted dry-run first. 11 Aug 09:00 PT looks OK — can you also send a calendar invite with dial-in?

— Jordan

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <j.hayes@novaretail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 12:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance validation protocol & reproducibility checklist

Jordan — quick clarifications from the engineering side: happy to run inside NovaRetail's VPC (we'll need a temporary key and the target cluster SSH/agent access). A few implementation details we want to lock down so runs are comparable: 

- Stabilization window: we'll report metrics from minute 4 through minute 10 (i.e., exclude first 3-minute ramp and last minute to avoid teardown noise). We'll include raw per-request timestamps so you can rewindow if desired.
- Cold-cache restart: restart command is in perf-harness-runbook.md (step 2.b) — exact snippet: `systemctl stop redwood-service && rm -rf /var/lib/redwood/kvcache/* && systemctl start redwood-service` — we will execute that from a non-root test user via sudo. We'll add the same snippet to the run README with the exact kernel args and container image digest for full reproducibility.
- Token accounting: we will include both model-side token counts and client-side reconstructed tokens; our CSV has columns: request_id, prompt_len, completion_len, server_first_token_ms, server_last_token_ms, p50,p95,p99.
- Warm-up traffic: warm-up uses deterministic sequence 1..100 from the prompt file with fixed seed; we will not include warm-up in steady-state metrics.

I'll attach the runbook patch and a short checklist in the shared repo. If you prefer, Ben can be the owner for post-run artifact handoff.

— Aisha
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
aisha.rahman@redwood.com

Jordan / Priya — perfect, thanks for the quick replies. Finalized action items and owners below before the 11 Aug run: 

Action items:
- Marcus: send calendar invite for 2026-08-11 09:00 PT with Zoom link + repo access (done after this mail).
- Aisha: publish patched perf-harness-runbook.md with the cold-cache restart snippet and the container digest; include reproducibility README with exact git hash. Deliverable by EOD 2026-08-06 (in flight).
- Ben: coordinate credentials exchange and ensure we have a temporary VPC test user for your infra team (Ben to request via email to infra@novaretail.com).
- Jordan / Priya: send the privacy/data handling note and confirm any prompt redactions by 2026-08-09.

Deliverables we'll hand you after the run:
- Raw harness logs (gzipped), aggregated CSVs, a README that lists the exact CLI invocation and env, and a short interpretation memo highlighting any SLO misses and recommended mitigations (batching/quantization suggestions).

If we agree to run in your VPC we'll need the SSH agent access and a test user; if hosted, we'll provide a pre-warmed snapshot and the same artifacts. Either way, we'll keep the runs reproducible by committing the harness config to the linked repo.

Thanks — I'll send the invite and repo link now. Looking forward to it.
